The Evidence Room

498A, Domestic Violence & False Case Judgments

Rulings on misuse of Section 498A, vague dowry complaints against a husband’s whole family, quashing of FIRs and chargesheets, and the limits of the Domestic Violence Act.

86 judgments · 37 from the Supreme Court · updated 25 November 2026

Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, now Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishes cruelty to a married woman by her husband or his relatives. The Supreme Court has upheld the law, but it has also warned many times that vague, general allegations against a husband’s whole family can turn a protective law into a tool for harassment.

The judgments on this page include rulings that quash FIRs and chargesheets built on omnibus allegations, decisions protecting distant and elderly relatives, arrest safeguards, the limits of the Domestic Violence Act, and cases holding that a false criminal complaint can itself amount to cruelty against the husband.

False Accusations Supreme Court
Piyush v. State of Maharashtra & Ors. (2026 INSC 1183)
November 2, 2026

Quashed a dowry-death and Section 498A case against a husband whose wife died by suicide in Toronto. No dowry complaint was made until after her death, her note blamed no one, and Canadian police found no foul play. Calling a wife ‘stupid’ or ‘useless’ cannot by itself amount to cruelty.

November 2026

False Accusations Madras High Court
R. Ramaswamy v. Regional Passport Office & Anr. (W.P.(Crl.) 2113 of 2026)
August 20, 2026

Set aside a passport-office order telling a husband to surrender his passport because his wife had filed a domestic violence case. A DV Act case stays civil until a protection order is breached, so it cannot justify revoking a passport. Neither spouse can be stopped from travelling abroad just because matrimonial litigation is pending.

False Accusations Supreme Court
Dr. Lokesh B.H. & Ors. v. State of Karnataka & Anr. (2026 INSC 784)
August 2026

Section 498A can extend to live-in relationships ‘in the nature of marriage’ — but only where there was a clear, provable intent to marry, not to every live-in relationship. The burden to prove that intent lies on the woman. Arrest safeguards from Arnesh Kumar apply strictly to this new category too.

Using these judgments

Official Court Copy opens the judgment PDF from the Supreme Court’s own website. Full Judgment opens the complete judgment text (Indian Kanoon, or a PDF copy of the order). Read Report opens a news or legal-blog summary where no full text is linked yet.

To rely on a judgment in court, cite it by its case number or citation; the court’s registry can issue a certified copy. Check that it has not been overturned or modified on appeal. The one-line summaries on this page are for information only and are not legal advice.

THE LAW IS ALREADY SPEAKING.

These courts ruled in our favour.
Now we need laws that don’t require a father to fight for years to reach them.
